newsitem.title: KENYA: U.N. appeals for $120 million for aid for Sudan.
newsitem.headline: U.N. appeals for $120 million for aid for Sudan.

text.p: The United Nations appealed on Tuesday for $120 million from donors for aid operations this year for more than four million victims of Sudans civil war.
The 4.2 million war victims, including 630,000 children under the age of five, are hit by chronic malnutrition and an alarming increase in disease, the U.N. Department of Humanitarian Affairs said.
"Persistent insecurity combined with natural disasters, including crop failures and floods in the Sudan have worsened the plight of almost all vulnerable groups," it added in a statement.
Sudanese rebels based in Eritrea launched an offensive on a string of government towns in the south and east in January.
The U.N. Childrens Fund needs $46 million, the largest slice of the appeal for health, nutrition and food for the wars main victims -- children, women and the elderly.
The U.N. World Food Programme requested $43.1 million for food aid for an estimated 2.6 million people in 1997, an increase of 500,000 from 1996.

Most aid for Sudan is sent through Operation Lifeline Sudan, a group of seven U.N. agencies and more than 50 others. Donors last year pledged $55.3 million, 52 percent of the total amount required, according to DHA.
